newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Birch sees NZ growth rate troughing at 2.3-2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Birch sees NZ growth rate troughing at 2.3-2.5 pct.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch said in Japan on Tuesday that he expected his country's growth rate at the trough of the current economic cycle to be around 2.3 to 2.5 percent.

In an interview monitored in Wellington, Birch told Reuters Financial Television that "it looks now as if, at the bottom of the cycle, the economy will still be growing at somewhere between 2.3 (and) 2.5 percent".
"We think that's not bad considering it's well above the sort of growth rates we used to average," he added.

The last Treasury economic update in December predicted that GDP would grow at a virtually unchanged rate of 2.6 percent in the year to March, following on from actual GDP growth of 2.7 percent in calendar 1996 as measured by Statistics New Zealand.
However, market consensus figures have consistently been below this level.
The government has insisted so far this year that it expects a soft landing followed by a rebound soon, but economists continue to say the trough has not yet arrived.
For 1997/98, the Treasury expects GDP growth jumping to 3.6 percent.
Birch made no direct comment on the likely timing of any trough in the cycle, but said "Our forecasts for growth are very positive".
"We expect the economy to continue to grow at about 3.0 percent this year and 4.0 percent next year, but there is a bit of a lag in terms of confidence," he noted.
Recent surveys of business confidence, in particular, have indicated that the current economic climate is seen as adverse.
Birch predicted that the government's continued confidence in future growth would be clearly expressed again in the budget.
